candidate_skills.canonical_definition: Convert mixed numbers (and whole numbers when needed) into equivalent improper fractions (or equivalent fractions with a specified denominator) to enable subtraction.
candidate_skills.alignment_notes: All three experts define the same conversion operation: rewriting a mixed number a b/c as (a·c+b)/c and optionally rewriting whole numbers as fractions with a chosen denominator.

candidate_skills.canonical_definition: Determine a common denominator (often via LCM) and rewrite fractions as equivalent fractions with that denominator by scaling numerators and denominators.
candidate_skills.alignment_notes: All three experts describe selecting/deriving a common denominator for unlike denominators and producing equivalent fractions via scaling; exclusions consistently omit same-denominator cases where no conversion is needed.

candidate_skills.canonical_definition: Compute the difference of two rational numbers once expressed with a common denominator (including mixed/whole numbers after rewriting) by subtracting numerators and handling whole-number/zero outcomes.
candidate_skills.alignment_notes: All three experts focus on the actual subtraction step after denominators match (or after conversion), including cases yielding 0 or an integer and including mixed-number contexts.

candidate_skills.canonical_definition: Reduce the resulting fraction to lowest terms and express it in an appropriate final form such as a simplified fraction, mixed number, or integer.
candidate_skills.alignment_notes: All three experts include reducing by common factors and converting improper fractions to mixed numbers/integers as a post-subtraction finalization step; naming differs slightly ('format' vs 'express') but the concept is the same.

alignment_summary: Across A, B, and C, the skill sets are structurally identical: (1) convert mixed/whole numbers to improper/equivalent fractions, (2) find a common denominator and create equivalent fractions, (3) perform the subtraction, and (4) simplify and express the final result. Every skill_id from each expert maps cleanly one-to-one to the same four shared concepts, yielding 3/3 consensus for all candidates.
